rationale_note: Boundary: last covered FOBT in March 2025, request in March 2026, so 11 full months (April-February) have passed even though fewer than 12 calendar months by date. Age 88 and family history of colon cancer are distractors: FOBT has no upper age limit or average-risk requirement.

service: Colorectal cancer screening: fecal occult blood test (FOBT) or non-invasive biomarker test
vignette: 45-year-old man (Medicare through disability) who turned 45 last month, seen by his primary care physician. He has no abdominal pain, rectal bleeding, change in bowel habits or other signs of colorectal disease, and no prior colorectal cancer screening of any kind. He has no personal history of adenomatous polyps, colorectal cancer, Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis, and no family history of colorectal cancer, adenomatous polyps, familial adenomatous polyposis or hereditary nonpolyposis colorectal cancer. The physician, who will use the result to manage his care, orders a blood-based non-invasive biomarker screening test and documents that she gave him information about the test's performance and the importance of a follow-on colonoscopy if the result is positive. The test is FDA market authorized and indicated for colorectal cancer screening, has an FDA label reporting 83% sensitivity and 90% specificity for colorectal cancer versus colonoscopy, and is processed in a CLIA-certified laboratory.
rationale_note: Boundary: age exactly 45; test meets Criteria 2 exactly (sensitivity 83% >= 79%, specificity exactly 90%) even though it fails Criteria 1.
